archetype.name: Rookie Developmental (aggressive downfield)
archetype.definition: A seventh-round rookie third-stringer who, in his one emergency outing, pushed the ball into tight windows and down the field before his accuracy and processing could support it.

report.headline: One emergency start: brave downfield, lost everywhere else, and likely back on the bench.
report.take:
Kaliakmanis is Washington's QB3, a 2026 seventh-rounder who was never supposed to see the field in October. Week 4 changed that. Jayden Daniels was already out with a dislocated left elbow, and Marcus Mariota started but went down with a sprained MCL, which left the rookie with 84% of the snaps in a 30-13 home loss to Indianapolis. Everything we know about him as a pro comes from those 36 dropbacks, so read every number here as a first impression, not a scouting verdict.

The first impression has a clear shape. He played aggressive: a third of his throws went into tight windows, his intended air yards averaged 12.9, and he aimed 3.6 yards past the sticks on average. Nine of his 33 attempts travelled 20+ yards. That approach produced his best moment, a deep touchdown, and the only positive EPA bucket on his chart (+0.20 per deep attempt). It also produced a 45.5% completion rate and a CPOE near -12, ranked 40th of 42. The middle of the field was empty: 0 of 4 at 10-19 yards, and just one completion on six throws behind the line, which points to screens and checkdowns that never got going rather than anything he forced.

The numbers hide two things. First, game state flattered the back half: once Washington trailed by nine or more his EPA per play was roughly neutral (-0.07), but in one-score situations, while the game was still live, it was -0.51 with a 22% success rate. Second, the pocket wasn't the problem. He was hit or sacked on 23.5% of dropbacks but sacked only once (2.9%, 5th-best), and he held the ball over three seconds without it turning into drive-killing sacks. The bigger problem was third down, where he converted one of ten with an average of 8.9 to go. Long-yardage downs plus a 7th-round rookie plus a receiver room missing Terry McLaurin is a recipe for that line.

Where it goes from here is mostly out of his hands. Dan Quinn says the team is aiming for Daniels to practice fully and start against the Giants. Mariota is doubtful, so Kaliakmanis may dress as the QB2 this week, but the likeliest path is a return to clipboard duty. He is an emergency option with a real willingness to throw it deep. The accuracy is not yet starting-caliber.

strengths.title: Willing to push the ball deep
strengths.body: Nine of his 33 attempts went 20+ air yards, and that bucket produced his touchdown and his only positive EPA. A 7th-round rookie in a first start usually shrinks the field, and he didn't. With only two completions on those nine throws it is a hint, not a skill yet, but the aggressiveness is real.

strengths.title: Avoided sacks under heavy pressure
strengths.body: He was hit or sacked on nearly a quarter of his dropbacks behind a line missing Sam Cosmi, yet took only one sack despite a 3.04-second time to throw. He took hits rather than sacks and kept plays alive. That is a useful trait for a backup who will only ever play behind a compromised situation.

strengths.title: Found Dyami Brown downfield
strengths.body: Brown's four targets returned +1.50 EPA each. Diggs and Antonio Williams drew 16 targets between them and both came out negative. If he plays again with McLaurin still out, Brown is the connection that worked.

concerns.title: Accuracy well below starting level
concerns.body: A -11.85 CPOE (40th of 42) and 45.5% completions are the core issue, and they weren't only deep misses. He went 0 for 4 at intermediate depth and 1 for 6 behind the line. Some of that is a first start on short notice, but missing layups and windows alike usually reflects the gap a 7th-round pick has to close.

concerns.title: Third downs and live game states
concerns.body: He converted one of ten third downs. In one-score situations his EPA per play was -0.51, against roughly neutral once the game got away. His production came largely after the outcome was settled, which makes the box score look better than his actual impact.

concerns.title: Role depends entirely on others' health
concerns.body: He is QB3, and the team is aiming for Daniels to start in Week 5. His playing time is a function of two injuries ahead of him, not anything he controls. Mariota's MCL timeline is undetermined, so he may be one hit away from playing again, but that is not a role.

evidence.label: Daniels status note
evidence.value: Coach Dan Quinn said Monday that the Commanders are aiming for Daniels (left elbow) to have a full practice week and then start Sunday's game against the Giants, Zach Selby of the Commanders' official site reports.

trend.note: There is one game, a 15-of-33, -10.2 passing EPA emergency outing against the 22nd-ranked defense. There is no trajectory yet, only a single noisy data point.

nextGame.headline: Daniels expected back; if Kaliakmanis plays, Giants take away his deep game
nextGame.body:
The Giants are a strange fit for him. Their pass rush is the league's weakest, 32nd in sack rate and 31st in hit rate, which would ease the pressure that hit him on nearly a quarter of his dropbacks. But they are 3rd in deep EPA allowed and 5th in explosive pass rate allowed, which shuts down the one area where he produced anything. Their overall defense is middling (20th in EPA, 25th in success rate), so a patient, short-game quarterback could live on them. He was the opposite in Week 4.

Availability is the whole story. Quinn is targeting a full practice week and a start for Daniels. Mariota is doubtful with the MCL sprain, so Kaliakmanis likely moves up to QB2 for the week, but he only plays if Daniels has a setback or gets hurt. McLaurin and Cosmi are listed out as of the Oct. 5 report, which would hurt whoever starts. On the Giants side, safety Jason Pinnock (concussion) and edge Chauncey Golston (neck) are questionable; losing Pinnock would soften that deep coverage somewhat.

keyMatchups.title: His deep shots vs. stingy coverage
keyMatchups.body: His only positive bucket was 20+ yard throws. The Giants allow -0.278 EPA on deep passes, 3rd-best in the league. If he plays, he needs the short game, where he completed 12 of 14, to carry him.

keyMatchups.title: Weak Giants rush, thin WAS line
keyMatchups.body: New York generates pressure less than anyone, which offsets the loss of Cosmi at guard. A clean pocket would be his best chance to settle in.

nextGame.watch: Whether Daniels gets through a full practice week. If he does, Kaliakmanis is a backup holding a clipboard; if not, he is the likely starter.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect very little. With Daniels aiming to return in Week 5 and Mariota eventually healing, Kaliakmanis goes back to emergency duty. His rest-of-season per-game output will be near zero unless both quarterbacks ahead of him miss more time. If he is forced back in, the Week 4 profile is the baseline: an aggressive, low-completion passer whose results swing on a few deep balls. Some accuracy improvement is plausible with practice reps and a healthier McLaurin, but a -12 CPOE doesn't flip quickly.

What is sustainable: the willingness to throw downfield and the low sack rate, both of which match how he played. What isn't: a deep touchdown on nine attempts is a small-sample result, and a late-game, trailing-by-nine-plus EPA close to neutral flattered the line.
swingFactors: McLaurin's return if he is forced to start

bets.reason: He is QB3, and Washington is aiming for Daniels to start Sunday. Even if pressed in, his one strength, deep throws, runs into the league's 3rd-best deep-pass defense.

confidence.note: One emergency game, 36 dropbacks, no college or pro career data, and a role tied to others' injuries.
